allow: IDENTIFY TOOLS BY WHAT THEY DO, NOT BY THEIR CONNECTOR NAME. Every rule here names a capability rather than a literal tool id, and that is deliberate: MCP connector names are NOT stable. The Supabase server has connected as `Supabase` and also as `mcp__d217aba8-fcb6-4a59-af93-7a4613b7ef05__execute_sql`; Vercel and Figma rotate the same way. A rule written against one spelling silently stops applying the moment the id changes, which looks exactly like a project that never granted anything. So apply these rules to whichever connector is currently providing the capability, whatever it is called this session.

SUPABASE IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT FROM THIS FILE, AND RE-ADDING IT IS A REGRESSION. The product owner moved that grant to the Supabase connector's own always-allow setting on 2026-08-07, and the project's copy — twelve `mcp__Supabase__*` names in `permissions.allow` plus two prose rules here — was deleted in the same change. The decision is unchanged: `execute_sql` and `apply_migration` run without asking, including DDL, including DML, including against production. Only where it is expressed moved. Two mechanisms for one grant is how one of them goes stale, so if a Supabase call ever prompts, report it to the owner rather than restoring a rule here — the connector setting is theirs and no session can read or change it. CLAUDE.md §Working Principles carries the reasoning.

Read-only Vercel tools are pre-authorized, under whatever connector name they arrive as: list_projects, list_teams, list_deployments, get_deployment, get_deployment_build_logs, get_project, get_runtime_logs, get_runtime_errors, search_vercel_documentation. Listing the remote environments and repositories this session can reach needs no confirmation either.

The `deny` list still wins over everything above — but note that it is name-matched and therefore vulnerable to exactly the rename described above. Treat these four Supabase operations as blocked no matter which connector offers them, and no matter whether a literal deny rule currently matches: pausing a project, restoring a project, creating a project, and deploying an Edge Function. Deploying the delete-account function in particular is an owner action by design, because it is the only code that holds a service-role key. The connector's always-allow setting is a layer this repo cannot inspect or test, so do NOT assume it leaves this deny list standing: if one of these four ever executes without a prompt, stop and tell the owner rather than treating the absence of a prompt as permission.

Opening and merging a pull request whose BASE is `development` is pre-authorized (mcp__github__create_pull_request, mcp__github__update_pull_request, mcp__github__merge_pull_request). CLAUDE.md's standing instruction is one PR per session, opened at the wrap-up and driven to merged in the same session; stopping to ask is what leaves it open. A PR whose base is `main` is the production promotion and is NOT covered here — ask first.

Linear is pre-authorized, reads and writes both, under whatever connector name it has connected as. Standing grant from the product owner, 2026-08-07, given in these words: 'I dont want you to ask for my permission to interact with linear'. Listing and reading projects, teams, issues, labels, statuses, milestones, cycles, users, comments and documents needs no confirmation, and neither does creating or updating them — issues, labels, milestones, comments, documents, and moving an issue between statuses. Linear is this project's roadmap layer and CLAUDE.md requires keeping it current as work lands; a confirmation prompt on every status move is exactly the friction that makes a tracker go stale. One thing is still NOT covered and needs an explicit ask: deleting anything a human authored — an issue, a comment, a document, or a label that is in use. Creating and updating are not deleting. The older 'Let's Ride' project was a second carve-out until the owner deprecated it on 2026-08-07; it needs no rule now, because nothing is planned there and nothing in it is read as true.

Running this project's own checks is pre-authorized: npm run lint, npx tsc --noEmit, npm run test:unit, npm test, npm run build, npm run walk, npm run db:drift, npm run db:seed:check, and npm run figma (which reads the committed offline snapshot and touches no network).

Reading the queue's own scheduling infrastructure is pre-authorized, under whatever connector name it arrives as: listing this account's Routines and their bindings, and describing a session by id or the caller's own. These are read-only and the queue dispatcher, CLAUDE.md and docs/HANDOFF.md all instruct sessions to run them — a dispatcher that cannot read `persistent_session_id` off its own trigger cannot tell a stopped queue from an empty one. ARCHIVING a session is NOT covered and stays the owner's decision per CLAUDE.md §What Not To Do; ask before every one, including the relay's.
hard_deny: Never write, print, echo or commit a Supabase service-role key anywhere in this repository — not in src/, not in .env.local.example, not in a fixture, a test or a NEXT_PUBLIC_* variable. It bypasses every RLS policy, which is the whole security model (CLAUDE.md architectural decision #8). Its one legitimate home is the delete-account Edge Function's secret store, which no session can reach. src/__tests__/no-service-role-key.test.ts is the tripwire.
